open_questions: His own words on his playing at length: the Modern Drummer interviews (2011 and earlier) and Rhythm's 2002 cover were not read; the quotes here come through Wikipedia, NBC News (quoting Rolling Stone and the AP) and Ultimate Classic Rock.

Who drums on which There Is Nothing Left to Lose song: the liner notes do not say; the Greatest Hits credits give Learn to Fly to Grohl and Breakout to Hawkins, and Hawkins names Aurora and M.I.A. as his.

The kits on each record: the Songsterr track names (Gretsch USA Custom, a Tama Starclassic on Times Like These, a Gretsch Broadkaster on Best of You) are the transcribers' labels; Wikipedia gives Gretsch from 2005 and Ludwig and Tama before.
Times Like These' riff: the tab writes 7/4, PAS hears alternating bars of 4/4 and 3/4; the drums are the same either way.

identity.name: Taylor Hawkins
home_scenes: Los Angeles (Topanga Canyon, then Hidden Hills)
identity.summary: Foo Fighters' drummer from 1997 until his death in 2022, behind a frontman who was a drummer himself: 'If he is the disciple of John Bonham, I'm a disciple of Stewart Copeland.' Roger Taylor's power and Copeland's energy in one rock drummer: open hats washing on the beat, the crash ridden through a chorus, a hard backbeat, the kick with the riff and often off the beat, and a run on the snare into every new part. Times Like These' riff in seven, Best of You's snare in 3 + 3 + 2, The Pretender's rimshots on every beat, Rope's kick off 1.

traditions.tradition: Queen and the Police: Roger Taylor and Stewart Copeland
traditions.impact: His 'first two major inspirations'; between them, a wide spectrum of rock drumming. He played along to records like News of the World.

traditions.tradition: Progressive and arena rock: Rush, Genesis, Van Halen
traditions.impact: Peart led him to Genesis and Phil Collins, 'a master'; Alex Van Halen among his classic rock heroes.

formative_events.event: Alanis Morissette's touring drummer, June 1995 to March 1997, in the videos for You Oughta Know and You Learn.
Volunteered when Grohl called him for a recommendation; Foo Fighters' drummer from 18 March 1997.
An overdose in London left him in a coma for two weeks; Grohl at his bedside. One by One was remade after it.

eras.label: The basement records
eras.context: Grohl's basement in Virginia: the 'jazzier' parts on There Is Nothing Left to Lose, then One by One remade in two weeks, the band's heaviest.

eras.label: The arena years
eras.context: Studio 606 West and Gil Norton: the big singles, a double album and Wembley Stadium.
defining_traits: the snare 3 + 3 + 2 under a tom or the ride

eras.label: Wasting Light and after
eras.context: To tape in Grohl's garage with Butch Vig, then Sonic Highways, Concrete and Gold and Medicine at Midnight.
defining_traits: the kick off 1 under a rimshot backbeat
the mid tom over the hat foot
a soca beat, a half-time chorus

swing.notes: Straight eighths and sixteenths throughout the ten songs.

dynamics.balance: Loud: a hard backbeat, often a rimshot, open hats and crashes; ghosts only here and there (All My Life, Rope).

feel_profile.interaction: Locked to Grohl's rhythm guitar first: the records start from the two of them (Wasting Light).

hand_techniques.name: open hats on the beat
hand_techniques.description: The hats opened on every beat, a wash under the verse (Times Like These, Long Road to Ruin, Run).

hand_techniques.name: rimshot backbeat
hand_techniques.description: The backbeat cracked on the rim (All My Life, The Pretender, Rope, Run).

hand_techniques.name: tom grooves
hand_techniques.description: The right hand on a tom in eighths in place of the hats: Best of You and Walk on the mid tom, Breakout on the floor tom.

hand_techniques.name: single-stroke runs on the snare
hand_techniques.description: Sixteenths on the snare from the "and" of 3 into each new part.

foot_techniques.name: hat foot under a tom groove
foot_techniques.description: The hat foot in eighths under the mid tom (Walk), on every beat under the snare (The Pretender).

foot_techniques.name: single foot
foot_techniques.description: One bass drum; pairs of eighths at 173 (The Pretender), the kick with the riff.

devices.description: Best of You's verse and Long Road to Ruin's bridge: the snare on 1, the 'and' of 2 and 4, a 3 + 3 + 2 of the bar in eighths, under the mid tom (Best of You) or the ride (Long Road to Ruin) in eighths, the kick between.
Run: the kick in a 3 + 3 + 2 of sixteenths in each half of the bar under the solo and the bridge; the chorus ends on the snare and the floor tom together in the same 3 + 3 + 2.
Best of You's interlude: the snare every third sixteenth from the 'a' of 1, five a bar, against the crash in eighths.

searched: The ten Songsterr tabs read section by section, Breakout to Run
Wikipedia (Taylor Hawkins and the six albums), PAS Playlist (2022), NBC News (2022)
devices_search.note: Three groupings, all in the groove and sourced to the tabs alone. Times Like These' riff in 7/4 is a meter, not a cross-rhythm.

voice_language.snare: A hard backbeat, often a rimshot; runs of sixteenths into a new part; the snare on every beat to lift a bridge.
voice_language.kick: With the riff: off 1 in Aurora and Rope, pairs of eighths in The Pretender, on every beat under Run's soca.
voice_language.toms: Grooves on the mid and floor tom in eighths; runs down them at a phrase's end.
voice_language.hihat: Eighths, or open on every beat as a wash; the hat foot under a tom groove.
voice_language.cymbals: The crash ridden in quarters through a chorus, crashes on the "and" of 4 to push; the ride's bell in pairs (Rope).

aesthetic: a cracking snare, open hats and big crashes
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Brilliant Zildjians, a lot of crash; the ride's bell played hard.

by_era.description: Big studio rock: a cracking snare, big crashes, a big room on In Your Honor.
Wasting Light to tape in a garage, a carpet under the kit to make it 'less loud and bright'.

sample_hints.1999-2007: Studio rock: a damped kick, a cracking snare, big crashes.
sample_hints.2002-2005, 2017: A big room for One by One, In Your Honor and Concrete and Gold.
sample_hints.2011: Big Rusty: thick and a bit rough, as Wasting Light was, to tape.

signature_traits.label: Open hats washing on the beat
signature_traits.description: The hats opened on every beat under a verse, the crash on 1 every other bar.

signature_traits.label: The crash ridden through a chorus
signature_traits.description: A crash on every beat in place of the hats, over the verse's kick.

signature_traits.label: The snare 3 + 3 + 2
signature_traits.description: The snare on 1, the "and" of 2 and 4 under a tom or the ride in eighths.

signature_traits.label: The kick off 1
signature_traits.description: A verse with no kick on 1: Aurora's on the "and"s, Rope's on the "and" of 1, the "e" of 2 and 3.

signature_traits.label: Joy at the kit
signature_traits.description: A grin through the whole set, limbs flailing; 'the engine behind it all' (Jordan Runtagh).

patterns.name: Breakout: the chorus
patterns.function: Open hats on 1, 2 and 3, the crash on 4, the kick on 1, its "and", the "and" of 2 and 3

patterns.name: Breakout: the interlude on the floor tom
patterns.function: The right hand on the floor tom in eighths, the high tom on the "a" of 2, the snare on 2 and 4

patterns.name: Aurora: the verse
patterns.function: Eighths on the hats, the kick on the "and" of 1, of 2 and of 3 and never on 1

evidence.note: Hawkins names Aurora, with M.I.A., as a good example of his playing on the album (Wikipedia, There Is Nothing Left to Lose).

patterns.name: Aurora: the chorus pushed
patterns.function: The crash on the "and" of 4, into the next bar

patterns.name: All My Life: the verse
patterns.function: Rimshots on 2 and 4 with a ghost before each; the kick off 1 one bar, on 1 the next, the hats opening with the snare

patterns.name: All My Life: the chorus
patterns.function: The ride on the beats, its bell on the "and" of 3, then on 1 and 3

patterns.name: Times Like These: the riff in 7/4
patterns.function: Eighths on the hats, the snare on 2, 4 and 6 with ghosts on the "a" of 2 and 4, a turn on the snare into the bar's last beat

evidence.note: The tab writes the riff in 7/4; PAS hears the band alternating bars of 4/4 and 3/4.

patterns.name: Times Like These: the verse
patterns.function: Open hats on the beat, the crash on 1, the kick on 1, its "and", the "and" of 2, 3, its "and" and the "and" of 4

patterns.name: Times Like These: the chorus
patterns.function: The second crash ridden in quarters over the verse's kick

patterns.name: Best of You: the verse
patterns.function: The snare on 1, the "and" of 2 and 4, a 3 + 3 + 2 of the bar in eighths, under the mid tom in eighths

patterns.name: Best of You: the chorus
patterns.function: The snare on every beat, the mid tom on the "and"s with the kick, the floor tom on 2, 3 and 4

patterns.name: Best of You: the interlude
patterns.function: The snare every third sixteenth from the "a" of 1, five a bar, against the crash in eighths

patterns.name: The Pretender: the first verse
patterns.function: Rimshots on every beat over the hat foot on every beat, the kick in pairs of eighths

evidence.note: The tab is written in half time at 87; here at the record's 173 in eighths.

patterns.name: The Pretender: the verse
patterns.function: Open hats on every beat, rimshots on 2 and 4, the kick in pairs

patterns.name: Long Road to Ruin: the bridge
patterns.function: The ride in eighths, the snare on 1, the "and" of 2 and 4, a 3 + 3 + 2 of the bar, the kick between

patterns.name: Rope: the verse
patterns.function: The kick off 1, on its "and", the "e" of 2, 3 and its "and", a rimshot on 2 and 4 and a ghost on the "a" of 2

patterns.name: Rope: the chorus
patterns.function: The ride bell two at a time, the ghosts between, the kick on 1, the "and" of 2 and of 3

evidence.note: PAS: 'a chorus groove paying homage to Neil Peart'.

patterns.name: Walk: the verse
patterns.function: The mid tom and the hat foot in eighths; the snare on 2 and 4, then on 2, the "and" of 3 and of 4

patterns.name: Walk: the bridge
patterns.function: The snare on every beat, the mid tom and the hat foot in eighths, the kick on the "and"s

patterns.name: Run: the verse
patterns.function: The kick on every beat under rimshots off it, on the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "a" of 3 and the "and" of 4, open hats on the beats

evidence.note: PAS: he adapts 'a soca beat' for most of the song.

patterns.name: Run: the chorus
patterns.function: Half time: the crash in quarters, a rimshot on 3 alone, the kick on 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "a" of 3 and the "and" of 4

patterns.name: Run: the solo
patterns.function: The kick in a 3 + 3 + 2 of sixteenths in each half of the bar, open hats on 1, 2, its "and" and 3

equipment.label: Gretsch USA Custom in black, Wembley Stadium, 2008
equipment.layout_notes: The Wembley film: a black Gretsch kit, chrome hardware, a white front head with the Gretsch script, brilliant Zildjian cymbals. Wikipedia: Gretsch from 2005, Ludwig and Tama before; Zildjian cymbals.

affiliations.name: Foo Fighters
affiliations.notes: From March 1997, after The Colour and the Shape; eight studio albums, There Is Nothing Left to Lose to Medicine at Midnight. Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, 2021.

affiliations.name: Alanis Morissette
affiliations.notes: Jagged Little Pill and Can't Not tours; Jagged Little Pill, Live (1997).

affiliations.name: Taylor Hawkins and the Coattail Riders
affiliations.notes: Drums and lead vocals; three albums, 2006, 2010 and 2019.

evidence.note: 'If he is the disciple of John Bonham, I'm a disciple of Stewart Copeland' (to Rolling Stone); one of his 'first two major inspirations', whom he 'idolized and eventually befriended'.
His other first inspiration: he played along to News of the World; 'Roger gave Queen their heavy feel and big sound'. Taylor talked him out of joining Guns N' Roses in 2000.
'One of my favorite drummers ever' (to the AP, 2009); through Rush to Genesis's Seconds Out: 'the man is a master'.
'It was thanks to Rush that I got into Genesis.' PAS hears Rope's chorus as 'paying homage to Neil Peart'.
Named among his influences (Wikipedia); Bonham was Grohl's model, Copeland his own.
Named among the classic rock drummers who influenced him (Wikipedia).
Jane's Addiction's drummer; Hawkins interviewed him as Rhythm's guest editor (Wikipedia).
Derek and the Dominos' drummer, named among his influences (Wikipedia).
Siouxsie and the Banshees' drummer, named among his influences (Wikipedia).
Foo Fighters' drummer after Goldsmith left during The Colour and the Shape; announced 18 March 1997.
Foo Fighters from 1997 to 2022, Grohl a drummer himself in front; the records start from the two of them 'locking in' (Wasting Light).
His son, a drummer, who played My Hero with the band at the Wembley tribute concert, 3 September 2022.
The SOS Allstars at Live Earth, 2007, with Roger Taylor and Chad Smith.

philosophy.idea: Learn by playing along to the records you love, as he did to Queen's News of the World.
Lock in with the rhythm guitar first; the song is built on the two of you.

innovations: A rock drummer's joy and power at stadium scale, Copeland's energy in an arena band

cultural_references.description: Rhythm magazine's Best Rock Drummer, 2005; Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Foo Fighters, 2021.
The Taylor Hawkins tribute concerts at Wembley Stadium and the Kia Forum, September 2022, with Roger Taylor, Stewart Copeland, Lars Ulrich, Travis Barker and his son Shane among the drummers.

common_misconceptions: That he drums on Everlong, My Hero and Monkey Wrench: they are Grohl's drums on The Colour and the Shape, recorded before Hawkins joined; Learn to Fly is Grohl's too.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A tight, bright studio rock kit with big crashes; a big room for One by One, In Your Honor and Concrete and Gold
generation_rules: Open hats on the beat under a verse, the crash on 1 every other bar.
The crash ridden in quarters through a chorus.
A hard backbeat, often a rimshot; a run of sixteenths on the snare into each new part.
The kick with the riff, off 1 when the riff is.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Stewart Copeland and Roger Taylor first, Phil Collins and Neil Peart after; Grohl's drummer for twenty-five years, and his son Shane after him.
